heatmaps.title: Homes permitted per 1,000 residents, by month
heatmaps.takeaway: Nationwide, 0.35 homes per 1,000 residents were permitted in 2026-08, vs 0.33 a year earlier.
heatmaps.source: Census BPS monthly state estimates (not seasonally adjusted), PEP

notes: State values use the ACS 1-year 2024; county values use the ACS 5-year 2020-24, so state and county figures are not directly comparable.
Owning vs renting: annual user cost of owning (2025 rates, prices and insurance) divided by 12 months of rent; above 1 means owning costs more.
Shortfall: housing needed for household growth since 2010 at a 6.58% normal vacancy, minus new homes and losses; negative values are a surplus. Counties end around 2022.
County shortfall is left blank where a county has fewer than 10,000 households or the estimate is within the ACS margin of error for households.
Heat maps: 2010 and 2024 match the ACS; other years are index-based estimates (median gap before adjustment 8% for values, 8% for income). 2026 is a partial year.
Insurance share: homeowners plus flood premiums divided by interest, property tax, upkeep and insurance (no risk premium, no appreciation).
Connecticut uses its 9 planning regions; their shortfall and 2015-19 permit baseline are not available. Puerto Rico is not included.
